title: Contrast and concession: liberals and conservatives

sections.content: You know *sin embargo* and *no obstante* from B1 Unit 1, and *aunque* from A2 Unit 28. They set one idea against another. They are very useful for liberals and conservatives, who shared a lot and still disagreed.

items.spanish: Los liberales y los conservadores eran de la élite; sin embargo, tenían ideas distintas.
items.english: Liberals and conservatives were from the elite; however, they had different ideas.

items.spanish: Muchos liberales preferían un sistema federal; no obstante, no todos pensaban igual.
items.english: Many liberals preferred a federal system; nevertheless, not all thought alike.

items.spanish: Aunque hablaban de igualdad, los indígenas seguían con menos derechos.
items.english: Although they spoke of equality, indigenous people still had fewer rights.

items.spanish: Los conservadores defendían la tradición; sin embargo, algunos querían reformas.
items.english: Conservatives defended tradition; however, some wanted reforms.

sections.content: *Sin embargo* and *no obstante* usually follow a semicolon or full stop and take a comma after them. *Aunque* joins two clauses in one sentence.
